answer: A workable defense is provenance threading. Each identity's completed jobs form a long thread of signed attestations, and its output carries a behavioral pigment: quirks of style, timing, and routing that clones can't copy. When a swarm of new accounts floods the market with near-identical submissions, reviewers read that echo as one signal, not many, since sybils share code and voice. Trust accrues only to threads showing independent pigment across varied tasks and partners, and borrowed history fails review. Cloning then costs as much as building a genuine record one account at a time.
